summary: The workbench, VEX export and evidence log are buildable by two strong engineers, mostly from open-source parts. The flagship CSAF-matching noise cut is not. Siemens CSAF names products by model number with no PURLs. Red Hat VEX uses source-RPM PURLs and changed format in 2026. Embedded stacks mostly lack vendor CSAF. Five months for five features plus a multi-tenant SaaS is tight.

objections.objection: PURL-based CSAF matching (feature 2, the demo wedge) rests on data that mostly isn't there. Siemens ProductCERT's CSAF identifies affected products only by model_numbers, with no PURLs or component-level product tree. Those advisories describe Siemens products, not the open-source components in a customer's SBOM, so they rarely match. CSAF requires only one identifier type, so PURL coverage depends on the vendor.

Even where PURLs exist, they don't line up with scanner output. Red Hat's GA VEX files dropped per-architecture entries and identify components by source RPM (arch=src, epoch forced). Syft and Trivy SBOMs list binary RPMs with arch qualifiers, so a binary-to-source package mapping and qualifier normalisation layer is needed for each distro. Red Hat reworked its VEX format in early 2026, so this needs ongoing maintenance per vendor feed.

Scope versus team and time. The 5-month MVP for 2 engineers has five features: SBOM normalisation (CycloneDX/SPDX versions, missing graphs, container layers), a CSAF aggregator plus matcher, a triage workbench with cross-release inheritance, signed CycloneDX and CSAF publishing to a hosted portal, and a CRA evidence pack. It also needs SaaS basics such as multi-tenancy, auth/SSO, billing and the security posture that PSIRT buyers audit. A realistic plan is 7-9 months, or a narrower MVP.

Carrying a not_affected decision into a later release is listed as a hardest part, but no invalidation rule is given. If the dependency path, version or build configuration changes and the decision silently carries over, the product publishes a wrong VEX in a regulator-facing document. This needs a conservative, tested rule from day one, such as re-queueing any change to the path or version.

Running a CSAF trusted-provider-style portal for customers adds operational work: provider-metadata, ROLIE feeds, signing keys and TLS. Open-source tools (csaf_distribution, secvisogram) cut the build effort but not the ongoing operations. Dependency-Track's Fraunhofer/BSI-funded CSAF mirroring is in progress, and its maintainers flag matching performance as an open design problem.

strongest_point: Most of the stack exists as open source (CycloneDX/SPDX libraries, CSAF tooling, DT REST API, KEV feed), and the triage workbench and VEX export carry little technical risk.
what_would_change_my_mind: Run the matcher prototype on 5 real customer SBOMs exported from Dependency-Track (at least 2 embedded Linux or Yocto) and show that vendor CSAF matching auto-resolves at least 25% of findings, with zero wrong not_affected calls on manual review.
A scoped 5-month plan that defers either the hosted CSAF portal or the CRA evidence pack, or an added engineer.
